Arithmetic for time points (mt_time)

Source: R/arithmetic.R
mt_time-arithmetic.Rd

Time points, linear (e.g. yearmonth()) or located cyclical (e.g. month_of_year(Sys.Date())), support:

  • Shifts: x + d, x - d and d + x shift by a duration(). Time points that don't exist (e.g. 31 January plus one month) are resolved with the mixtime.on_invalid option; see time_shift().

  • Shifts by chronons: x + n and x - n shift by n of the time points' own chronon.

  • Differences: a - b is a duration() in their finest common chronon.

Located cyclical time shifts its underlying time, and its position within the cycle follows. For underspecified cyclical time, see mt_cyclical_free-arithmetic.

A discrete time point spans its whole chronon, so shifting by a duration finer than its chronon, or taking differences between discrete time points of different chronons, is an error. Any other combination, such as adding two time points or subtracting a time point from a duration, is also an error.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'mt_time'
e1 + e2
# S4 method for class 'mt_time'
e1 - e2

Arguments

e1, e2

Operands, at least one a time point (mt_time) vector.

Value

A time point vector for shifts, a duration (mt_duration) for differences.

Examples

x <- yearmonth("2024-01")
x + months(2)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] 2024 Mar
x + 0:3
#> <mixtime[4]>
#> [1] 2024 Jan 2024 Feb 2024 Mar 2024 Apr
yearmonth("2024-05") - x
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] 4.0 months
date("2024-01-31") + months(1)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] 2024-02-29
month_of_year(yearmonth("2024-11")) + 3L
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] Feb
try(date("2024-03-15") + hours(3))
#> Error : Cannot shift 1 day time points by 3 hours, the result is temporally
#> indeterminate.
#> ✖ A discrete 1 day spans a period of time that doesn't shift as a whole by 3
#>   hours.
#> ℹ Shift by a duration that 1 day nests within or that is a multiple of 1 day,
#>   or use continuous time.
